label: 2026 Orbital Launches
delta: As of July 14: 84 Falcon-family launches in 2026 (83 Falcon 9 + 1 Falcon Heavy) — SpaceX President Gwynne Shotwell projects ~140-145 Falcon 9 launches for the full year. 600th flight-proven-booster launch: Starlink 10-45 (July 14, 09:10 UTC, SLC-40 Cape Canaveral, B1080 28th flight, ASOG 161st landing, 638th booster recovery overall). Record 36th single-booster reflight: Starlink 10-42 (July 9, B1067, SLC-40, ASOG 160th landing, 635th recovery). Transporter-17 rideshare (July 7, Vandenberg, 81 payloads incl. first commercial nuclear cubesat, 1,800th+ cumulative rideshare payload). Twin Starlink launches 8 hours apart July 13-14 from opposite coasts. Previously: 71st Starlink + Starshield (June 7, Vandenberg SLC-4E, 21 Starlink V2 Mini + 2 Starshield sats, OCISLY 622nd landing).

label: Total Booster Recoveries (All-Time)
delta: 638th: ASOG landing (Starlink 10-45, July 14, SLC-40 Cape Canaveral — B1080 28th flight; SpaceX's 600th flight-proven-booster launch overall; ASOG's 161st touchdown). 635th: ASOG landing (Starlink 10-42, July 9, SLC-40 — B1067's record 36th flight; ASOG's 160th touchdown). 622nd: OCISLY landing (Starlink + Starshield, June 7, Vandenberg SLC-4E). 621st: ASOG landing (Starlink 10-43, June 4, SLC-40 Cape Canaveral — B1090 12th flight; ASOG's 153rd touchdown). 620th: OCISLY landing (Starlink 17-47, June 3, Vandenberg SLC-4E). 619th: OCISLY landing (Starlink, June 1, Vandenberg SLC-4E — B1088 16th flight; OCISLY's 200th touchdown — drone ship's second century milestone). Note: IFT-12 Booster 19 (May 22) was NOT recovered — off-nominal boostback burn caused transonic ocean impact at ~1,450 km/h.

label: Starlink Satellites in Orbit
delta: ~10,759+ working satellites in orbit as of July 11, 2026 (~12,472+ total ever launched, per Jonathan's Space Report). SpaceX filed an FCC application July 6 for up to 100,000 Gen3 satellites across two new VLEO shells with W-/D-band frequencies, positioned as AI-data-center backhaul infrastructure in addition to consumer broadband. S-1 confirms 10.3M subscribers (doubled YoY); ARPU $66/month (Q1 2026). First 10,000-in-orbit milestone crossed May 25, 2026; public 10,000 milestone reached early June 2026.

label: Starlink Subscribers
delta: 10.3M subscribers confirmed in S-1 filing (doubled YoY). Starlink segment profit: $1.2B in most recent quarter. 160+ countries served. ARPU: $66/month Q1 2026.

label: Max Single Booster Reflights
delta: B1067 set a new record with its 36th flight on the Starlink 10-42 mission (July 9, 2026, SLC-40 Cape Canaveral) — the first orbital booster in history to reach 36 flights. Previously: 34th flight on Starlink 10-44 (Mar 30, 2026).

label: Starship Integrated Flight Tests
delta: FAA CLEARED Starship to resume flights July 13, 2026, closing the IFT-12 mishap investigation: root causes were heat effects on propulsion components during ascent and erroneous engine alarm settings that prevented Booster 19's reignition. SpaceX modified reignition sequencing and alarm thresholds. IFT-13 (Booster 20 V3 + Ship 40 V3) STACKED and targeting launch 22:45 UTC July 16, 2026 from OLP-2 — first flight to carry 20 operational V3 Starlink satellites; Booster 20 to attempt a Gulf of Mexico splashdown (not a tower catch), Ship 40 to attempt a Raptor relight and Indian Ocean splashdown. Outcome pending as of this update. Prior: IFT-12 completed May 22, 2026 — Raptor relight in space (first ever) and Ship 39 Indian Ocean splashdown succeeded, but Booster 19 was lost to an off-nominal boostback burn (transonic ocean impact, not recovered), triggering the FAA grounding.

label: SPCX (Nasdaq) — Post-IPO Trading
source: SEC EDGAR S-1 / CNBC / TechCrunch / Nasdaq
contestNote: IPO COMPLETED: priced at $135/share (555.56M Class A shares) June 11; Nasdaq (SPCX) debut June 12 — largest IPO in history at a $1.77T implied valuation. Underwriters exercised the 'greenshoe' overallotment June 15, lifting total proceeds to $85.7B. Stock surged as high as $225.64 (all-time high, June 16) before a steady pullback; SPCX joined the Nasdaq-100 July 7 in the fastest index inclusion on record (~$4.3B passive inflows), despite only ~4% public float. On July 15, shares fell below the $135 IPO price for the first time (as low as $132.15 intraday, closed $135.27) — a fourth straight down day, attributed to profit-taking and valuation reassessment rather than a single catalyst. Morningstar values SpaceX at ~$780B (55% below ask); New Constructs: needs $1.1T revenue by 2035 to justify price. Musk holds ~42% economic equity, ~79-85% voting control (dual-class Class B) — cannot be removed as director except by his own vote. S-1 financials: 2025 revenue $18.7B (+33% YoY), 2025 net loss $4.94B, accumulated deficit $41.3B. Starlink: 10.3M subscribers, $1.2B segment profit.
